subject: Urgent: ClearMap throughput/loss spike — rapid mitigation plan
messages:
From: Erin Blake <erin.blake@clearmap.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: support@clearmap.ai
Date: Mon, 27 May 2029 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Unexpected latency + errors starting 13:20 UTC — urgent

Hi Stephanie / Lauren,

We started seeing a sharp degradation in ClearMap's production inference starting ~13:20 UTC today. Symptoms: p50 unchanged, p99 jumped from ~220ms to ~1.1s, 5xx error rate climbed to ~2.4% and sustained for ~20 minutes, and our throughput dropped by ~28% on the busiest endpoint. This is directly impacting our customers' upload flow.

We did not push code on our side. We noticed the spike shortly after Redwood rolled what looked like a cache/serving knob change on 12:58 UTC (per the audit email). Can you confirm whether anything non-routine was changed for our tenant or model routing?

Attached: support_log_20290527.tar.gz (server logs + request ids). We need a mitigation plan and ETA for restoration — this is high severity for us.

Thanks,
Erin
Erin Blake
Head of Platform
ClearMap AI

From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Erin Blake <erin.blake@clearmap.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 May 2029 14:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency + errors starting 13:20 UTC — urgent

Erin — thanks for the heads-up and the logs. We're on it.

Immediate plan:
- I've looped in Ben (serving/runtime) and Monica (CS/ops) to triage KV cache eviction and queueing metrics now.
- Can you confirm the most-impacted endpoint(s) and a couple of request ids from the attached archive you want prioritized? That will speed retrieval.

Short ask for your team: If you can leave traffic patterns unchanged for the next 30 min, we will attempt a targeted mitigation (no tenant-wide restart) and update at 15:00 UTC. If we need to do a short traffic throttle or swap model variant, we'll ask first.

I'll stand up a 30-minute working call at 14:30 PT / 21:30 UTC (invite to follow).

—Stephanie
Stephanie Nguyen
Account Exec, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Erin Blake <erin.blake@clearmap.ai>
Date: Mon, 27 May 2029 14:33:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency + errors starting 13:20 UTC — urgent

Quick diagnostic summary (live run):
- KV cache eviction rate for tenant clearmap: spike started 12:59 UTC, eviction/s rose ~18x vs baseline.
- Prefetch queue size for high-priority lane increased and we observed HOL (head-of-line) blocking: long-running prefetches occupied hot lanes, blocking small low-latency ops.
- Token-serving queue for their busiest model showed tail latency amplification when eviction + prefetch backlog coincide — aligns with p99 spike.
- We see increased batching backpressure and a small surge of LRU churn that matches the error window.

Immediate mitigations executed (14:28 UTC):
1) Reduced max_prefetch for ClearMap from 64 -> 8 for 30m window (soft change, no restart).
2) Temporarily promoted tenant to protected priority lane (prevents aggressive evictions from other tenants).
3) Deployed a temporary cache pin for top-500 prefixes for the endpoint (reduces cold-lookups).
4) Enabled conservative per-tenant kv-throttle for write-heavy tails.

Observed effect (14:32 UTC): p99 dropped from ~1.1s -> ~350ms, 5xx rate down to 0.6%, throughput recovered to ~92% of previous baseline. Continuing to monitor.

Next steps (15:00 UTC follow-up call):
- If stable for 45m, we will roll the prefetch cap into a longer policy (tunable) and propose a permanent per-tenant protection profile.
- Engineering will generate eviction snapshots and a short incident slab (kv_eviction_snapshot_20290527.csv attached) for postmortem and recommended config defaults.

Notes: root cause appears to be a combination of sudden prefix churn (customer request distribution change) + an unfortunately timed autoscale of prefetch aggressiveness that amplified LRU churn. We should review autoscale triggers that allow high prefetch scaling on highly-skewed prefix distributions.

--Ben
Ben Carter
Senior SRE, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
Attachment: kv_eviction_snapshot_20290527.csv

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Erin Blake <erin.blake@clearmap.ai>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 28 May 2029 09:45:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Unexpected latency + errors starting 13:20 UTC — urgent

Erin / ClearMap team —

Thanks for your patience and for the logs. Ben's mitigations improved user impact quickly; we'll keep the protections in place while we complete a brief postmortem and recommend durable config changes.

Next items we own (ETA and owners):
- Full postmortem + recommended runtime defaults (Ben) — deliver by 2029-05-30 EOD
- Proposed per-tenant protection profile (priority lane + default prefetch cap) (Monica) — draft by 2029-05-29
- Review of autoscale triggers on prefetch policies and a safety gate to prevent high-prefetch scaling under heavy prefix skew (Engineering leadership) — kickoff 2029-05-29

If anything degrades we will escalate to execs and consider a brief model-variant throttle to buy time. For now, please confirm if you need a scheduled follow-up call tomorrow to review the postmortem draft.

Appreciate the prompt reporting — we'll follow up with the incident doc and the eviction snapshot attached for your records.

Lauren Bishop
Head of Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
